findings.evidence: Artin.lean:136-141 — its own docstring says "This is the integral-lattice counterpart of `TauCeti.ClassFunction.indCharacterSpan`"; `indCharacterSpan` is at Spanning.lean:247 with the parallel lemmas at 262 and 270. Artin.lean imports Spanning (line 10), so the move is strictly to an earlier file. grep shows no use of `indCharacterSpanInt` in `natCard_nsmul_one_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic` or `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic`.
findings.fix: Move the definition and its two universal-property lemmas into `Induction/Spanning.lean`, in the existing `### Characters induced from a family of subgroups` section next to `indCharacterSpan` / `ind_ofCharacter_mem_indCharacterSpan` / `indCharacterSpan_le_iff`, and update the module docstrings' `Main definitions` lists. The three comparison theorems with `indVirtualCharacters` (lines 246-301) genuinely need both `Spanning` and `Ideal` and may stay in `Artin.lean`.
findings.issue: `indCharacterSpanInt` (plus `ind_ofCharacter_mem_indCharacterSpanInt` and `indCharacterSpanInt_le_iff`, lines 147-168) is stated for an arbitrary family `P`, has no Artin- or cyclic-specific content, and is not used by any theorem in this file; it unfolds only to `indCharacterSet` (Spanning.lean:233). Its predecessor `indVirtualCharacterSpanCyclic` was cyclic-specific and so belonged here; the generalized version does not, and a downstream elementary-subgroup (Brauer) development would have to import `Induction/Artin.lean` to get it.

summary: New bundled induction maps and the single-subgroup hom are in their natural homes and all three new imports are used and minimally scoped. But `indCharacterSpanInt` and its two API lemmas are family-general, depend only on `indCharacterSet` from the earlier `Spanning.lean`, and are unused by Artin's theorem, so they should not live in `Induction/Artin.lean`.
